modes.label: Plain TLS
modes.keyHolder: prover holds the whole session key
modes.trust: no one — a raw TLS transcript is unusable as proof
modes.reason: TLS authenticates plaintext with a symmetric key the prover also holds — so it can rewrite the response and re-MAC it.

modes.label: MPC-TLS
modes.trust: the notary did not collude with the prover
modes.reason: Keys are derived in 2PC; neither side holds the full key, so the prover can't re-MAC a forgery alone.
modes.cost: ~30 MB preprocessing · ~5 s native / ~10 s browser · ~40 round trips

modes.label: Proxy-TLS
modes.keyHolder: prover holds the key; proxy sees only ciphertext
modes.trust: a single proxy/witness did not collude with the prover
modes.reason: The proxy pins the ciphertext in flight; keys are revealed afterward, so a forged response won't match.
modes.cost: no preprocessing · ~1.6 s native / ~2.0 s browser

modes.label: TEE-TLS
modes.trust: the TEE manufacturer (Intel/AMD) and no side-channel break
modes.reason: The TLS client runs in an attested enclave that signs what it saw; the prover never holds the key.
